name: fs-operation-scope-enforced
body: Law (prose; assessed by review): a filesystem operation (`apg_rm` / `apg_mv` / `apg_cp`) may touch ONLY a path granted by the acting agent's EFFECTIVE `permission.edit` scope — the source path, and for mv/cp the destination path as well. The TOOL enforces this: it reads the acting agent's `edit` rule set (its ALLOW and DENY entries) from its agent permission block (via the opencode plugin context), evaluates the entries in order with the LAST matching entry winning (a path matched by no entry is refused; deny-by-default), resolves the rule set and the candidate path in ONE consistent frame, and refuses a path outside that scope; enforcement does not live in the permission layer's matching of the tool's path argument. The fs scope EQUALS the `edit` scope, so a `deny` the `edit` permission honours also refuses the fs operation — an allow-only fs scope that ignored deny was the feedback-14 escape. The boundary is the PROJECT WORKTREE: for a code-writer, a path that resolves into the main checkout (outside every project worktree) is refused regardless of the caller-supplied directory, and no operation may cross the project/worktree boundary. The capability is never granted as a blanket `""*"": allow`: the grant is deny-by-default with the role's owned globs allowed under `apg/.worktrees/*/` only. The tools perform plain filesystem operations only — they are not `git rm`/`git mv` — and they never mutate graph nodes (that is `apg node rm` / `apg edge rm`).
